vo_01a.text: I'm Chris. Some afternoons I want to get outside, but I never know where to go.

vo_01b.text: And my friends? Total homebodies. 'We should hang out' never becomes a plan.

vo_02.text: So I built StrollCall. Map apps need a destination. StrollCall starts from how you feel: tell it how long you have and what you're in the mood for, and it plans a walk worth taking, solo or with a friend.

vo_03.text: I just say it. Muse Voice transcribes it, and Muse Glimmer, Meta's open-weights model running on my own H200 on Modal, reads it in about half a second, six and a half times faster than the API. And my location never goes to any model.

vo_04.text: And it doesn't stop at directions. While I walk, the map fills the screen, and my buddy listens. Mid-walk, I ask for a coffee stop: Muse Spark calls a tool, the planner re-routes, and only real, open places come back.

vo_05.text: Walking is better together. One link, no app, no sign-up. My friend taps once, and says what they'd like too.

vo_06.text: Muse Spark balances both of our wishes and explains the trade-off. Splitting the distance isn't fair: the map's midpoint leaves us 4.8 minutes apart. StrollCall splits the walking time instead: just 0.6 minutes apart, an eight-times smaller gap.

vo_07.text: Under the hood, our own walking graph of New York: 139,106 points from OpenStreetMap, planning a walk in about 29 milliseconds. Four Meta models do the human side: Muse Glimmer reads wishes, Muse Spark negotiates and ranks, Muse Image draws the invite, Muse Voice listens.

vo_08.text: And unlike a typical chatbot, it's built not to make things up. Every evaluation is pre-registered. 12 out of 12 test pairs, all correct. Meta's reading caught every wish, 10 of 10, where keyword rules caught 7. And a checker throws out any claim our data can't back up.
